questions.question: How do you call func area(width w: Double, height h: Double) -> Double?
questions.why: Callers use the argument labels width and height; w and h are only used inside the function.

questions.question: What does _ mean in func double(_ n: Int)?

answers.text: There is no argument label, so you call it double(4)

questions.question: What must a guard … else { } block do?

answers.text: Run the rest of the function
Leave the current scope, for example with return

questions.why: guard is for early exits, so Swift requires the else block to leave.

questions.question: What is the type of numbers inside func sum(_ numbers: Int...)?
questions.why: A variadic parameter arrives as an array.

questions.question: When is inout the right choice?

answers.text: Whenever a function returns more than one value
Whenever a function needs a parameter
Rarely: when a function must change a variable that belongs to its caller

questions.why: Returning a new value is usually clearer; inout is for the few cases where changing in place is the point.
